title: Hazel and the Orbit
premise: Ada Almeida keeps the Meridian Beacon, a deep-space relay whose founding records have been quietly erased, and she likes it that way: a woman without a past, tending a station without a history. When the freighter Calloway's Wake returns from a nine-year run with its crew biologically younger than when they left, Ada is sent to investigate the 'impossible accident'—and finds the ship's logs scrubbed, its passengers terrified, and evidence of eleven crew members who no longer exist. As the corporation that owns the route moves to destroy the ship and everyone who touched it, Ada discovers the beacon itself was built to hide the same atrocity, and that her own erased past is tangled in it. In the end she broadcasts the truth through the beacon no one remembers commissioning, chooses the ragged found family of survivors over her safe invisibility, and finally claims a name—her real one—that the record can never again take from her.
about_author: Beatrix Whitlock is a former maritime insurance adjuster who spent a decade reconstructing disasters nobody wanted remembered before turning to fiction. She writes from a converted lighthouse on the Atlantic coast, where she insists the fog improves her prose.

chapters.title: The Light Nobody Ordered
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. She performs her meticulous maintenance rounds aboard the Meridian Beacon, revealing her ritualized invisibility and her habit of investigating anomalies no one assigns her. A routine query about the beacon's origin returns a void in the archives—the first crack. Emotional beat: lonely competence masking a fear of being seen.

chapters.title: Nine Years Younger
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The freighter Calloway's Wake docks unscheduled, its crew visibly decades younger than their service records. Corporate dispatch orders Ada to classify it as an insurance anomaly and send them on. Instead she boards. Emotional beat: curiosity overriding a lifetime of careful non-involvement.

chapters.title: Passengers of the Impossible
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, intercut with engineer Sef Okafor's testimony. The crew remembers a voyage they cannot reconcile with their bodies; Sef recalls an eleventh crewmate the manifest denies. Ada notices the logs have been rewritten with surgical precision—by someone with beacon-level access. Emotional beat: dread taking root.

chapters.title: What the Manifest Forgets
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. He walks Ada through the ship, showing her a cabin sealed from inside, personal effects belonging to people not on any list, and a child's drawing taped to a bulkhead. The crew calls the missing ones 'the unmanifested.' Emotional beat: grief for people the paperwork says never lived.

chapters.title: A Woman Without a File
chapters.summary: Corporate auditor Ilsa Vane arrives aboard, charming and lethal, and pulls Ada's credentials—which are suspiciously perfect, too clean, as if authored rather than accumulated. Vane offers Ada promotion for a quiet report. Emotional beat: Ada recognizes her own erasure technique used against her.

chapters.title: The Backward Clock
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. She traces the temporal signature: the ship passed through something near coordinates matching the beacon's original survey charts—a chart older than the beacon's supposed construction date. The beacon was built to watch that place. Emotional beat: the vertigo of realizing her home is a blindfold.

chapters.title: Eleven Names
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Under sedation-assisted recall, the crew collectively recovers fragments: a distress call answered, a colony station found gutted, eleven volunteers who went across—and were made to never have existed. Sef remembers his sister among them. Emotional beat: mourning sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Terms of Settlement
chapters.summary: Vane's POV. She reports to Halcyon Route Authority that the anomaly is contained, recommending the Wake be scuttled with all hands as a navigational hazard. We see her genuine belief that erasure is mercy. Emotional beat: chilling bureaucratic certainty.

chapters.title: Salvage Rights
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada secretly copies the corrupted logs onto the beacon's core, using the station's forgotten architecture as a vault. She realizes whoever built the beacon designed it to preserve what others delete. Emotional beat: first sense of kinship with the beacon's vanished maker.

chapters.title: The Maker's Handwriting
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Deep in the beacon she finds engineering habits identical to her own—same idiosyncratic welds, same private notation system. The builder taught her, or was her. Her amnesia has edges now. Emotional beat: identity trembling like a held breath.

chapters.title: Interdiction
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Halcyon ships arrive early, citing a reactor fault, and order immediate evacuation—to vessels under their control. Sef stalls; Ada cuts the docking clamps and puts the Wake into a slow drift only she can navigate. Emotional beat: the point of no return, chosen freely.

chapters.title: Ghosts in the Relay
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Hiding in the beacon's dead channels, the fugitives find archived transmissions: the eleven unmanifested crew calling for help, recordings Halcyon believed destroyed. Among the voices, one speaks in Ada's private shorthand. Emotional beat: horror and recognition braided together.

chapters.title: The Massacre That Isn't
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. The crew debates: broadcast and be hunted, or stay hidden and let the dead stay dead. Sef argues they owe the eleven existence, even posthumously. Ada, asked to decide as investigator, refuses to decide alone—for the first time sharing weight. Emotional beat: found family forming under pressure.

chapters.title: Vane's Ledger
chapters.summary: Vane's POV. Boarding the beacon legally, she finds Ada's hidden vault but hesitates at the child's drawing from the Wake, which matches a memory Vane has of a case she closed long ago—her first erasure. Emotional beat: a crack in the true believer.

chapters.title: Countdown at Meridian
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Halcyon sets a demolition timer disguised as a solar-storm advisory. Ada must choose: flee with the survivors or stay to hand-crank the ancient transmitter through the storm window. Sef and the crew refuse to leave her. Emotional beat: invisibility finally, gratefully abandoned.

chapters.title: What the Beacon Was For
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. In the vault she finds the founder's final log: the beacon was commissioned by the massacre's survivors—including Ada herself, who wiped her own memory to survive infiltration. She didn't forget her mission; she became it. Emotional beat: devastating self-reckoning, then fierce clarity.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Climax, multiple POVs. Under fire and storm, Ada transmits everything—the eleven voices, the altered manifests, the temporal signature—at beacon power, burning out relays one by one while Sef reroutes and Vane, defecting, feeds her Halcyon's counter-frequencies. Emotional beat: sacrifice transformed into testimony.

chapters.title: The Whole Sky Listening
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, dazed aftermath. The transmission propagates; independent stations, rival insurers, and colonists begin verifying the eleven names independently. Halcyon's demolition order collapses under public record. The Wake drifts safe. Emotional beat: exhausted, disbelieving triumph.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. At the inquiry, the crew testifies; Vane corroborates, surrendering her ledger. Sef reads his sister's name into the record and watches it stick—no longer deniable. Emotional beat: grief given permanence at last.

chapters.title: Rebuilding the File
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Offered reinstatement, commendation, a new clean identity, Ada declines them all. Instead she begins writing her own record—messy, contradictory, hers—and formally registers the beacon under its founders' names, including her forgotten one. Emotional beat: authorship of self.

chapters.title: Hazel
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. In the founder's log she finds her birth name: Hazel Almeida, the girl who survived. The crew, now living aboard the repaired beacon as its new keepers, christen the restored main relay after her. She answers to it without flinching. Emotional beat: belonging, claimed not granted.

chapters.title: Keepers of the Light
chapters.summary: Ensemble coda. One year on: the beacon trains its light on the anomalous coordinates openly, a watchdog instead of a blindfold. Hazel teaches Sef's niece the maintenance rounds; Vane sends coded warnings of other erased places. Somewhere, another impossible ship is coming home. Emotional beat: vigilance as love, ending on open horizons.
